tradeoff_detail.loses: Requests to api.x.ai and api.together.xyz now route through Router like api.openai.com/api.anthropic.com; any vendor-specific response headers/fields Router doesn't pass through are lost, and the request briefly transits Router's infra before reaching the vendor (xAI) or Router's own hosting of the open model (Together models), vs. going direct.

Together AI traffic (togetherai provider) now goes through Router's /v1/responses translation instead of directly to api.together.xyz; for the three default Together models (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, GLM-5.3-Flash, Kimi-K3) Router serves the same open weights from its own backend rather than Together's infrastructure, so Together-specific latency/throughput characteristics and any Together response metadata are lost. Non-default/未-cataloged Together models fall through to Together unchanged.

The shared OpenAI-compatible branch (serves togetherai already handled above, xai, groq, openrouter, lmstudio, ollama, custom) now passes routerOptions() in all cases, but only api.x.ai is unlocked as a host: xai calls for grok-4.3/4.5/grok-build-0.1 route through Router to the same xAI backend (billing/observability only, no backend change). groq.com and openrouter.ai hosts are intentionally not unlocked (see kept claims); ollama/lmstudio (loopback) and arbitrary custom endpoints are never matched by the host allowlist, so they are unaffected.

PR title/body generation's fallback branch (non-openai.com baseUrl) now passes routerOptions() too; it only takes effect when the configured provider's baseUrl is api.x.ai or api.together.xyz (the two hosts unlocked on this repo), in which case it loses the same things as the base.ts togetherai/openai-compatible branches (vendor-specific backend/metadata, see those claims). Every other configured provider (groq, openrouter, ollama, lmstudio, custom) is unaffected -- its PR generation call still goes straight to that provider.
